name: Napier NZ Deco
summary: A distinctive Art Deco style in Napier New Zealand following the 1931 earthquake.
description: It features geometric patterns, stepped forms, and decorative elements characteristic of Art Deco with local adaptations. This style emerged after the 1931 earthquake when the city was rebuilt in the fashionable Art Deco style of the period.
culturalContext: Napier, New Zealand — flattened by the 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake — rebuilt itself in three years as the world's most complete Art Deco city: Louis Hay's residential Deco, local interpretations of Miami Beach and Zigzag Moderne, Maori motifs in friezes, all limestone-white against the Pacific. The 1930s rebuild (2,000 buildings, £21m) made "Napier Deco" a tourism brand (annual Art Deco Weekend), with the ASB Bank (1933) and Daily Telegraph as photographed icons.
